meta.cite: Barton O. Oliver's mTOR Atlas (live data, not an archived version; give corpus_snapshot and source_commit). doi:10.5281/zenodo.22059963

data.mechanism: Unphosphorylated 4E-BP1 clamps onto eIF4E and stops it assembling the cap-binding complex. mTORC1 phosphorylates 4E-BP1 to release that grip - so the brake on translation is released, not the accelerator pressed.
data.mechanism_beginner: Untagged 4E-BP1 clamps onto eIF4E and blocks it; mTORC1 tags 4E-BP1 to make it let go – releasing a brake, not pressing an accelerator.
data.boundary: Biochemical and cell-culture evidence (in vitro assays, mammalian and mouse cells, plus one review). It establishes the binding switch itself. It does not measure how much translation changes in a given tissue, in whole animals or in people.
